issues.title: Missing equality leaves the lower anomaly-conductivity bound undefined

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same result can be proved for $\sigma_a^m>\sigma_{bg}^M$, with similar arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: Without the missing equality, sigma_a^m is not assigned the essential infimum of sigma_a. Consequently, the inherited high-conductivity alternative and the proof's assertion that the lemma also holds in that alternative use an undefined parameter.
issues.overall_effect: The high-conductivity branch of lem:mainl and subsequent bounds involving sigma_a^m are not literally well-defined. The low-conductivity branch using sigma_a^M is unaffected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the omitted equality and define σ_a^m = ess inf_{x∈Ω} σ_a(x). No other part of the high-conductivity branch needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The parallel definitions of the other conductivity bounds and the subsequent scalar use of σ_a^m uniquely force the missing equality. This is a transcription error requiring no mathematical inference or change of guarantee.

issues.title: The monotonicity estimate has reversed signs and bounds
issues.failure_explanation: In the proof's case sigma_1=sigma_D<sigma_bg=sigma_2, eqn:in1 bounds a nonnegative NtD quadratic form above by a negative integral. Its next claimed implication, eqn:lem1, consequently does not follow. The valid estimate uses sigma_2-sigma_1, with the unweighted integral as the lower bound and the sigma_2/sigma_1-weighted integral as the upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of lem:mainl and the later power bounds derived from its monotonicity estimate are unsupported until the displayed inequality is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eqn:in1 by ∫_Ω(σ₂−σ₁)|∇u₂|² ≤ ⟨(Λ_{σ₁}−Λ_{σ₂})g,g⟩ ≤ ∫_Ω(σ₂/σ₁)(σ₂−σ₁)|∇u₂|², leaving the ensuing proof unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The monotonicity property, the ordering σ_D<σ_bg, the immediately following positive lower bound, and the correctly oriented specialization later in the old source uniquely determine this correction. The proof already reasons with the corrected estimate, so only the transcribed signs and order in the display must be fixed.

issues.title: Weak UCP is falsely stated for an arbitrary subset

failure_location.quote: If $u$ is constant in $A$, then $u$ is constant in $\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims that constancy on any subset implies global constancy. A smooth nonconstant harmonic function is automatically constant on a singleton, so the claim is false under its stated hypotheses. The supported UCP formulation used in v3 requires constancy on a ball, and the anomaly application correspondingly needs an interior ball.
issues.overall_effect: The blanket UCP assertion and its use to exclude nontrivial kernel data are unjustified unless the constancy region has nonempty interior. The intended application to open anomaly domains can be retained after adding that condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the UCP for a nonempty open constancy region, or equivalently for a ball B contained in Ω, and explicitly use that each anomaly domain contains such a ball when excluding nonzero kernel data.
issues.why_classification: This adds the standard local premise omitted from the UCP statement. It is a short, routine correction that preserves the theorem's intended use for open anomaly domains, as well as the kernel argument and all resulting guarantees; no new proof mechanism is needed.

issues.title: The implementation thresholds potential instead of power density
issues.failure_explanation: Following the printed implementation step forms a sublevel set of the squared scalar potential rather than of the ohmic power density. Those functions generally have different level sets, so the step does not implement eqn:thr2 or the preceding Kernel Method construction.
issues.overall_effect: The executable reconstruction instruction can return a different region from the power-density algorithm analyzed in the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace σ_bg|u_bg(x)|² by σ_bg|∇u_bg(x)|² in the implementation's sublevel set.
issues.why_classification: The preceding definition of power density, eqn:thr2, and every earlier description of the method uniquely require the gradient. Inserting ∇ makes the instruction implement the already specified algorithm without changing any reasoning or guarantee.

issues.title: The perturbation proposition allows non-self-adjoint noise
issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:pert invokes an indexed real-eigenvalue perturbation bound while eqn:noise assumes only that N is bounded. For a self-adjoint clean operator with two eigenvalues, a sufficiently large bounded skew-symmetric perturbation on their span produces nonreal eigenvalues. Thus the ordered eigenvalues required by the proposition are not defined for all admitted inputs.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue bound and the ensuing selection of a decreasing noisy spectrum lack their required spectral setting for the stated noise model.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the perturbation N to be bounded and self-adjoint before applying the ordered-eigenvalue bound. Equivalently, preprocess arbitrary measured data by taking its self-adjoint part and apply the proposition to N_s=(N+N*)/2, for which ‖N_s‖≤‖N‖.
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local spectral qualification, and the old numerical noise model is already symmetric. Adding the premise or symmetrizing the data restores real ordered eigenvalues and the perturbation estimate through a short routine step, without changing the method, rate, or intended noise regime.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: where $N$ is a bounded and self-adjoint operator, and $\delta=\norm{N}$

issues.title: The noisy threshold uses a clean eigenpair identity

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, let $g_n$ to be an eigenfunction $g_n$ of $\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}$, then
Find the eigenvalues $\lambda_k$ and the eigenfunctions $g_k$ of $\Lambda_n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old noisy procedure has access to an eigenpair of Lambda_n, whereas eqn:thr is derived from P-P_b=lambda_n||g_n||^2 for an eigenpair of the noise-free operator. For measured data the correct identity contains the unknown term -<Ng,g>, bounded only by plus or minus delta||g||^2. Hence the old noise-independent threshold interval is not justified for the pair selected by the algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed threshold bounds, and therefore the noisy reconstructed region selected from them, have no guaranteed relation to the clean anomalous power. The noise-free construction is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For a noisy eigenpair (λ̃_n,g̃_n), use ⟨(Λ_{σ_D}−Λ_{σ_bg})g̃_n,g̃_n⟩=λ̃_n‖g̃_n‖²−⟨Ng̃_n,g̃_n⟩ and |⟨Ng̃_n,g̃_n⟩|≤δ‖g̃_n‖². Propagate the resulting lower and upper factors (λ̃_n−δ)_+ and λ̃_n+δ into the anomalous-power and threshold bounds.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and follows from a short perturbation calculation, so no global reconstruction is required. Nevertheless, it materially replaces the old noise-independent threshold guarantee by a noise-dependent interval whose relative width can be order one for the eigenvalues selected near the noise floor. A recognizably comparable noisy algorithm survives, making the loss limited rather than major.

issues.title: An integrated-power coefficient is used as a pointwise level
issues.failure_explanation: The old construction claims that the pointwise threshold epsilon equals alpha times the eigenvalue quadratic form merely because the integral over D is bounded by multiples of that form. Total power does not determine a pointwise density level: different spatial distributions and set measures can have the same integral. Thus eqn:thr does not follow from eqn:sogp3 and does not determine the claimed sublevel reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: Even for noise-free data, the stated pointwise threshold and therefore the selected sublevel set are not determined by the proved integrated-power bounds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the pointwise level from the integrated-power coefficient. Define D_τ={x:p_n(x)<τ}, choose a total-power coefficient c in the conductivity-derived interval, and determine τ by the one-dimensional cumulative-power condition ∫_{D_τ}p_n dx=cλ_n‖g_n‖², with an explicit tie convention if a level set has positive measure. Use this τ in the reconstruction.
issues.why_classification: Total power cannot be converted into a pointwise level by the printed proportionality. A complete repair can retain the sublevel-set method through a contained threshold reoptimization, consistent with the old source's later integral-search instruction, but it replaces the advertised explicit level formula and can change the selected region. This exceeds a routine same-formula correction while avoiding global proof architecture and major mathematical loss.
